Portable hydrokinetic turbine for 0.5-1.0 m/s streams: low-flow redesign (v4)

Scope and status. Everything in this package is model prediction and design intent. No part has been printed, machined or tested; no GL60 has been measured; manufacturer web pages (cubemars.com, genasun, bluerobotics.com, digikey) could not be reached from this session, so the generator values are the ones listed in the brief and in the earlier review, bracketed by sensitivity cases. Every number below is written by docs/make_report_v4.py from the result files of the scripts in model/, cad/ and tools/.

1. Executive summary and feasibility verdict

  • What the GL60 can deliver (model, baseline assumptions, arrangement A, buck-boost MPPT): net 12 V electrical power 0.16 W at 0.5 m/s, 0.49 W at 0.6, 0.96 W at 0.7, 1.60 W at 0.8, 3.45 W at 1.0 m/s (12.0 W at 1.5, 27.2 W at 2.0). One-at-a-time sensitivity envelope: -39 % / +14 % at 0.7 m/s and -12 % / +8 % at 1.0 m/s (hydrofoil polars at Re 4e4-8e4 from an XFOIL surrogate, unmeasured friction and generator constants; section 8). Over a 24 h day at 0.6-0.8 m/s that is roughly 12-38 Wh: enough to keep a phone or a headlamp charged, not a camp power supply.
  • Minimum flow. The rotor sustains rotation and the converter accepts power from 0.5 m/s (the 5 V minimum input of the converter and the fixed friction are the limiters; at 0.4 m/s the bus would be below 5 V and the net output negative). Self-start from rest is NOT predicted at 0.5 m/s under the baseline model. The starting torque is the BEM torque at TSR 0.1 with induction (the no-induction flat-plate estimate used in the first draft was 1.8x too high and is kept only as an upper bound): at 0.5 m/s the rotor makes 29 mN m (upper bound 51) against a breakaway of 36 mN m (assumed GL60 cogging 24 mN m + seal + bearing). Model minimum self-start: 0.6 m/s baseline, 0.4 optimistic, 0.8 pessimistic (0.5 with the upper-bound torque). A start at 0.5 / 0.6 / 0.7 m/s needs the measured cogging to be below 17 / 30 / 45 mN m. Once turning, the rotor sustains itself from 0.5 m/s (cogging averages out), so a hand spin at deployment covers the gap; gates G1 (cogging) and G6 (starting torque) decide it.
  • The winding resistance is not the obstacle. At these powers the torque is tens of mN m, so copper loss is 0.1-3.5 % of the available hydraulic power below 1 m/s. The obstacles are, in order: rotor efficiency at Reynolds numbers of 4e4-8e4 (Cp 0.25-0.33), the fixed friction torque (seal + bearing + motor no-load, 7 mN m plus no-load loss), the generator voltage (only 5.0 V at 0.5 m/s: a boost-capable converter is mandatory; a rectifier straight into the 14.4 V battery produces nothing below 0.8 m/s and only 0.50 W there), and the converter's own minimum input voltage and quiescent draw.
  • A gearbox does not help. A 2:1 stage (optimistic 96 % per stage, +5 mN m running, +8 mN m breakaway) changes net output with the selected buck-boost by -69 % at 0.5 m/s, +1 % at 0.7 and +8 % at 1.0 m/s, and raises the self-start threshold of the feasibility study's representative rotor from 0.8 to 0.9 m/s (the extra breakaway is a fifth of the 0.7 m/s starting torque): rejected; direct drive is kept.
  • Selected rotor: 3 blades, NACA 4412 blending to NACA 4418 at the root, Schmitz planform for design TSR 1.5 scaled x1.0, root chord 50.1 mm, maximum chord 60.0 mm, tip chord 31.1 mm, root twist 32.7 deg, solidity 0.41; it runs at TSR 2.8-3.1 (129-291 rpm over 0.5-1.0 m/s). Against the previous 1-2 m/s blade on its drum hub it delivers 2.7x at 0.6 m/s and 1.41x at 1.0 m/s; against the original rev-2 blade placed on the same small hub it gains +749 % at 0.5 (net; +46 % in peak shaft power), +34 % at 0.6, +10 % at 0.7 and -4 % at 1.0 m/s: the gain is where the brief asks for it, and the two blades are within 4 % of each other over 0.8-1.0 m/s (the new blade gives up 13 % at 2.0 m/s).
  • Recommended mounting: arrangement A (rotor on a short 316 shaft ahead of a stationary sealed nacelle). The hub radius drops from 48 to 28 mm, which is worth +77 % at 0.7 m/s and +44 % at 1.0 m/s against the same blade in the hub-integrated drum (B), and the 8 mm seal halves the seal friction. The price is depth: 136 mm operating, which packs as two pieces of 72 mm (rotor assembly with its own shaft, unscrewed at the M5 joint) and 75 mm (nacelle including the captive stub shaft and the penetrator nut); the shell clamp, three struts and three ring arcs pack flat (thickest part 61 mm). The 76 mm target is met packed, not operating.

3. Optimisation methodology and objective function

  1. Polars (model/polars.py): NeuralFoil (XFOIL surrogate, Ncrit 9) on a 29 x 10 (alpha, Re) grid for NACA 4412 / 4415 / 4418, SG6043, E387, FX63-137 and E818, Viterna-extended to +-90 deg for the standstill estimate. E387 (confidence 0.84) and E818 (0.64, coarse database coordinates) are reported but not selectable. Experimental polars at Re 4e4-8e4 are not available to this project.
  2. BEM (model/bem_lowflow.py): Prandtl tip and hub losses, Buhl high-induction correction, per-element Reynolds number, root blend to the 18 % thick section over the inner 35 % of span, nacelle inflow deficit factor 0.85 inboard of r 38 mm for arrangement A (assumption), vectorised Ning residual solved by bisection. Cross-checks: the near-inviscid limit stays below Betz (Cp 0.43 with tip/hub losses), P = omega Q, and the v3.1 blade evaluated with both the old analytic polar and the new tables agrees within the polar uncertainty (the thick root is the difference).
  3. Coupled operating point (model/generator_lowflow.py): rotor torque curve against friction (seal, bearing, motor no-load, hub windage) and the generator (KV 21.5, Kt 0.444 N m/A, R 5.5 ohm, L 2.72 mH, 14 pole pairs, Schottky bridge 2 x Vf(I), commutation overlap as a reactive voltage drop), then the converter (efficiency eta_max - k/P_in, quiescent draw, minimum input voltage, and either a boost-with-clamp or a buck-boost input window). The MPPT law picks the bus voltage (= rotor speed) that maximises converter output inside the window; it is required (BOM 26) never to command more than the 1.35 A rating. Starting torque = the BEM torque at TSR 0.1 with momentum induction (baseline); the no-induction estimate (alpha = 90 deg - twist, W = V, Viterna polars) is 1.6-1.8x higher and is reported only as an upper bound (review C1); breakaway = cogging + seal + bearing breakaway. Dynamic friction and breakaway are separate.
  4. Objective: J = sum over V of w(V) P_net(V) with P_net = 0 where the candidate cannot self-start, cannot sustain rotation along the unloaded path to its operating point, or sits below the converter's 5 V input. Two weightings: uniform over 0.5-1.0 m/s (six flows) and low-flow-weighted {0.5: 0.3, 0.6: 0.3, 0.7: 0.2, 0.8: 0.1, 0.9: 0.05, 1.0: 0.05} (illustrative, not measured). Also tracked: the same without the self-start gate ("hand-started") and with cogging 8 / 40 mN m.
  5. Design space (model/optimize_blades.py): stage 1 = 384 candidates: 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 blades x four airfoils x design TSR 1.5-6 (Schmitz planform at the airfoil's best-L/D angle at the local Reynolds number) x chord scale 0.7 / 1.0 / 1.3 (chord capped at 60 mm). Stage 2 = 124 refinements around the leaders (3 / 4 / 5 blades x design TSR 1.5 / 1.75 / 2 / 2.5 x chord scale 1.0 / 1.3 / 1.5 x pitch -3 / 0 / +3 deg, plus two-blade and SG6043 checks). Selection (selection.json): the mean of the two normalised objectives (self-start gate inside the objective, baseline starting torque = BEM at TSR 0.1), subject to >= 12 deg of printed hub wall between adjacent pockets (pocket arc from the root chord and twist on the 28 mm hub); ties go to the lower solidity. The best candidate without the self-start gate is recorded separately.

Reading. Two blades give the best Cp per unit solidity; four and five blades reach their starting torque earlier but lose Cp to profile drag at these Reynolds numbers. Low design TSR (1.5 for the pick; 1.5-2 for the whole top group) wins because the wide chords raise the local Reynolds number (the chord is the only lever on Re at a given flow) and the starting torque, while the actual Cp peak sits at TSR 2.6 and the coupled MPPT point at TSR 2.8-3.1, where the GL60's voltage is highest for the torque it must absorb. The low-Reynolds sections lose in the coupled result despite their better 2-D L/D: their higher design lift coefficient produces narrower chords (lower Re) and a sharper Cp peak. The objective surface is flat near the optimum (the top eight stage-2 candidates lie within 1.5 % of each other on J_uniform), so the hub-packaging constraint (>= 12 deg of printed wall between pockets) decided among near-equal candidates: the pick scores 98.7 % of the best unconstrained J_uniform and 97.4 % of the best J_low-flow (unconstrained best: {'B': 4, 'airfoil': 'naca4412', 'lam_d': 1.5, 'c_scale': 1.3, 'c_max': 0.06, 'dbeta': -3.0}).

5. Selected blade geometry and why it won

3 blades, NACA 4412 outboard blending to NACA 4418 over the inner 35 % (printability and root bending), Schmitz planform at design TSR 1.5 x1.0 (capped at 60 mm), root eased to 85 % at the hub, elliptical tip taper to 55 %, pitch offset -3 deg, 1.0 mm blunt trailing edge. Station data: model/selected_design.json (chord 50.1 -> 60.0 -> 31.1 mm; twist 32.7 -> 10.6 deg). Figures 5 and 6 compare it with the previous designs. It won because it (i) has the highest gated objective: under the baseline starting-torque model it self-starts from 0.6 m/s (at 0.5 m/s it makes 29 mN m against 36 mN m of breakaway; the TSR >= 3 designs start later still), (ii) has the highest coupled output at 0.5-0.7 m/s once turning (Reynolds effect of the wide chord), (iii) stays within 4 % of the original rev-2 blade over 0.8-1.0 m/s, and (iv) fits 3 pockets on a 28 mm hub with 31 deg of wall between them. What it gives up: about 13 % at 2.0 m/s against the rev-2 blade and a higher standstill drag (thrust at 2 m/s 38 N at the operating point).

Load control. Below the clamp voltage both converters regulate the bus, i.e. the rotor speed, so the generator cannot stall the rotor: the equilibrium sits on the stable side of the torque peak (fig. 9). With the boost-only converter the bus is clamped at the battery above about 1.5 m/s; the rotor is then held at a fixed speed and, from 1.8 m/s (interpolated on a 0.05 m/s grid), the clamp current exceeds the GL60 rating: a boost-only unit needs a 1.5-2 A limiter or a 40 V relay dump for the 1-2 m/s survivability case. The buck-boost keeps regulating to 2 m/s (1.27 A at 23.0 V). Open circuit at 2 m/s is 46 V: below the 60 V TVS standoff and the converter's 60 V input. Current and temperature: copper loss is 0.02 / 0.15 / 0.70 W at 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0 m/s and 8.8 W at 2 m/s inside a sealed nacelle. Thermal limits are not the sizing case below 1.5 m/s; the earlier v3.1 heat-path analysis applies if the device is left in a 2 m/s flow (rear cap in 6061).

seal service pull the hub (one screw), press the seal from the wet face partial disassembly (v3.1 plan)

Load path (A, fig. 10a). Thrust: blade -> airfoil tongue (clamped between the two hub halves by an axial M3) -> hub -> 316 washer -> circlip A (DIN 471-8) -> rotor shaft -> its shoulder on the stub's front face (the M5 joint is in tension only under handling loads) -> stub shaft -> collar B (between the seal and the bearing) -> 608 inner race -> outer race -> DIN 472-22 internal ring in the cap boss -> cap plug and flange -> front flange -> front lip of the shell clamp -> three L-struts -> guard ring and stake. Reverse load: DIN 471-8 circlip behind the bearing (0.3 mm end play) -> inner race -> outer race -> bearing press fit (N7) in the boss; the rear flange is held by the shell's rear lip; the only forward loads are handling and a snagged cable. Assembly order: seal pressed from the wet face; stub in from the dry side (collar B passes through the 22 mm bore, the 8 mm journal through the seal with a bullet); bearing pressed over the tail to collar B; DIN 472-22 ring; rear circlip; dog hub pinned; caps into the tube; shell clamp closed (4x M4). Rotor: circlip A and washer on the rotor shaft, hub halves and blades bolted, nose screw and plug; the rotor screws onto the stub (M5, right-hand: the generator reaction torque tightens it; Loctite 222) and unscrews for packing. The mechanical review (M-C1..C4, M-M1..M11) found the first draft's integral collar A and collar-inside-the-seal layout uninstallable, the cap bore without a thrust shoulder, the dog coupling not engaging, the hub and both caps unretained and the packing claim false (captive shaft); this is the corrected arrangement. Single rotor bearing (review M4, accepted with analysis): the rotor's centre of mass sits 38 mm ahead of the bearing centre; the radial clearance of a 608 (0.005-0.012 mm) allows 1.4-3.4 mrad of tilt, i.e. 0.20-0.48 mm at the blade tip, 0.035 mm at the seal lip and 0.032 mm at the dogs (0.2 mm radial clearance), with the rotor thrust pre-loading the bearing axially; the GL60 therefore stays radially unloaded and gate G5 measures the tip motion (a second bearing, 698 in a 7 mm longer boss, is the fallback). Hub retention: the M3 nose screw clamps the hub between its 13 mm washer on the hub floor (10.4 MPa under 0.5 N m) and circlip A (0.38 MPa on the hub rear face at 2 m/s thrust). Hub bolts: M3 x 40 in 7.5 mm counterbores from the nose surface, 7 mm washers at both ends, nylocs in 5.5 mm rear pockets, 0.2 N m (11 MPa under the washers). Stake socket: 40 mm engagement, 4 mm wall, 1.7 MPa peak bearing pressure under 7.2 N m (device drag taken as 1.25x the rotor thrust at 2 m/s); guard ring 6 mm wall, 0.14 mm/N in-plane compliance against a 5.4 mm tip gap (gate G10). Minimum deployment depth with the socket below the ring is about 0.35 m (socket mouth + 30 mm of exposed stake + ring + 50 mm freeboard); a two-stake yoke or a base plate is the shallow-water alternative (not designed). Torque: hub D-bore -> shaft D-flat -> cross-pinned dog hub -> TPU disc (two dogs, 0.2 mm radial clearance) -> GL60 bell; the stator is screwed to the rear cap. The GL60 carries no rotor thrust and no radial load. The motor is dry: tube, one EPDM O-ring per cap, an 8 mm PTFE lip seal on the polished 316 journal, a WetLink M10 penetrator and an M6 vent; IP45 is irrelevant inside that boundary. Penalties quantified: the seal and bearing take 7 mN m of the 38 mN m the rotor makes at 0.5 m/s (19 %) and 4 % at 1.0 m/s; the assumed nacelle inflow deficit costs 1.8 / 1.7 / 1.8 % of peak Cp at 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0 m/s (to be checked in G8/G11); the hub ratio 0.28 costs the annulus area shown in the feasibility table.

Minimum self-start / sustain velocities: baseline 0.6 / 0.5 m/s; optimistic (upper-bound starting torque, cogging 8 mN m, seal x0.5, Re x1.5, Glauert-Spera) 0.4 / 0.4; pessimistic (cogging 40 mN m, Re/1.5, uncorrected momentum, 0.30 W converter overhead, seal x2) 0.8 / 0.6; baseline with the upper-bound starting torque 0.5 / 0.5. Net power in the pessimistic combination: 0.00 / 0.53 / 2.75 W at 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0 m/s; optimistic 0.30 / 1.24 / 4.01 W. A self-start at 0.5 / 0.6 / 0.7 m/s requires the measured GL60 cogging to be below 17 / 30 / 45 mN m (gate G1). The sweep evaluated candidates with 40 elements and a 0.5 TSR step; the selected design is re-evaluated here with 50 elements and a 0.2 step, which moves its numbers by 0.4 % at most over 0.6-1.0 m/s; "root chord" is the chord at the first element centre (r 28.7 mm). The sustain floor is the converter's 5 V minimum; a 3 V converter would move it to 0.5 m/s with 0.17 W at 0.5 m/s.

Converter overhead and generator convention (reviews M5, M6). The converter's fixed overhead (gate drive, housekeeping, quiescent) is assumed 0.13 W; it takes 48 % of the DC power at 0.5 m/s, and with 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.50 W of overhead the net output at 0.5 m/s is 0.09 / 0.00 / 0.00 W (0.7 m/s: 0.89 / 0.79 / 0.59 W): the 0.5-0.6 m/s numbers are conditional on a converter with <= 0.15 W of overhead (gate G9). The generator convention (V_oc,dc = rpm / KV with KV 21.5 from the listed 516 rpm at 24 V) is 4.5 % optimistic against a 3-phase bridge average; if the listed "KV 25" is rpm per volt of line-line peak EMF, the rectified constant is about 26.2 and the output falls to 0.08 / 0.87 / 3.08 W at 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0 m/s. Gate G1 measures V_dc/rpm through the bridge.

9. Reproducible source code and CAD exports

model/polars.py (polar tables), bem_lowflow.py, generator_lowflow.py, feasibility.py, optimize_blades.py (stages 1-2 and the selection), coupled_eval.py (figures 2-9, comparison, sensitivities); cad/make_v4.py (parametric assembly, STEP per part, assembly STEP, print-oriented STLs with the blade meshed as a closed structured surface), cad/views_v4.py (figure 10); tools/qa_gates_v4.py. Exports: out/v4_assembly.step, out/v4_*.step (37 parts, 16 printed, 5 machined), out/v4_*_PRINT.stl (13 files, all closed, blade mesh within 0.07 % of its STEP volume, tilted -4.0 deg for a level pressure face). Regenerate in the order given in README.md. Print notes: blades pressure-side down on a raft with full tree supports under the pressure side (the review measured 4,228 mm2 of down-facing surface inside 45 deg and a 27 mm2 line of bed contact: the twisted blade cannot be levelled; the alternative root-down print puts the root bending across the layers, 1.9 MPa against the assumed 2.7 MPa interlaminar allowable), 100 % infill, layers along the span; hub halves parting face down (the pockets print as bridged tunnels: gate G3 uses the real hub half), no supports; TPU disc flat; shell halves on the parting plane; struts on the flat of the leg; ring arcs on an end face (each arc fits a 220 mm bed; scale the arcs 100.5 % for ASA shrink and check the tip gap). Fasteners modelled: hub bolts, hub screw, circlips, rings, pin; listed but not modelled: shell M4 x 35, strut M4 x 12 + inserts, ring M3 x 10 + inserts, stator screws. Minimum blade thickness 3.7 mm at the tip (12 % of 31.1 mm), 1.0 mm trailing edge.

Structural screening at the 2 m/s survival case (model/structure_v4.py; allowables assumed: ASA 8 / 4.5 MPa long-term in-plane / across layers, 15 / 8 short-term, 2.7 / 4.8 interlaminar shear): rotor thrust 37.8 N (12.6 N per blade) and 0.55 N m at 704 rpm, runaway 999 rpm. Root bending 1.89 MPa in the 9.0 mm thick NACA 4418 root (in-plane for a flat print); centrifugal 20 N per blade (26 g) -> M3 bolt double shear 1.4 MPa, tongue bearing 0.48 MPa, 4.2 mm ligament shear-out 0.17 MPa; pocket walls take the flap moment at 1.03 MPa; the three pockets span 89 deg each, leaving 31 deg of hub wall (8.7 mm at the pocket floor, 15.2 mm at the surface); strut legs 2.9 MPa in bending; shaft torsion 5.5 MPa (8.2 at the D-flat; 316 yield ~200); 608 bearing Fa/C0 0.027. All below the allowables with margin; fatigue (3/rev strut wake) is not assessed.

10. Independent adversarial review and corrections

Independent adversarial review and corrections (v4 low-flow turbine)

Three reviewer agents, each a separate model instance with its own scratch directory and no write access to the package, reviewed the exported first draft (commit 2add8bd): (1) hydrodynamics / BEM / electrical, (2) mechanical / CAD / deployment, (3) model implementation and numerics. They re-computed numbers independently (own scripts under /home/user/review_v4_*). Their findings, the corrections and the re-verification on the regenerated results are listed below. "Independent" here means a separate reviewer instance and separate re-computation, not a separate physical method or an experiment: nothing has been measured.

M-M1 mech major Hub bolts could not be fitted: the 3.4 mm holes exited the nose obliquely with no head seat (the counterbore line was dead code), the modelled bolt started inside solid material, and the nut pocket (6.0 x 3.2) was smaller than an M3 nyloc + washer; at 0.5 N m the 7 mm washers would load the ASA to 28 MPa. 7.5 mm counterbores from the nose surface to a seat 3.5 mm ahead of the hub body; 7.5 x 5.5 rear nut pockets; M3 x 40 with 7 mm washers at both ends at 0.2 N m; bolts, washers, heads and nuts are modelled and in the clash check. regenerated: counterbore 7.5 mm to x -17.5, nut pocket 7.5 x 5.5 mm, bolt length 40.0 mm; washer pressure 11 MPa at 0.2 N m
M-M2 mech major The WetLink M10 bore, the M6 vent and the lead channel lay on the stator's hole lines (0 / 180 deg): a section at x 88.5 showed the holes at (0, +-20) and (0, +-25) merged into the penetrator and vent voids, so two screws per pattern had no material; with the stator 1.0 mm from the cap, the penetrator's dry side, the splice and the 6 mm cable had no room. Penetrator at r 19 on the 45 deg line (22 mm counterbore, 4 mm wall to the O-ring groove), vent at 225 deg, lead channel deleted; stator-to-cap gap 4.5 mm with a 20 x 4 splice pocket in the cap centre; an ASSUMED 12 x 3 mm inner protrusion of the penetrator is modelled and clash-checked against the stator. regenerated: nearest stator hole centre to the penetrator centre 15.0 mm (wall 2.7 mm); penetrator protrusion to stator 1.5 mm
M-M3 mech major Neither cap was retained in the tube (only O-ring friction): the test plan's +20 kPa leak test would push 83 N on each plug, and a snagged cable would pull the rear cap out; the clamp did not touch either flange, so the thrust path 'tube -> clamp' was friction only. Full-length printed shell clamp (two halves, 4x M4 lugs) whose end lips trap both cap flanges (now 80 mm diameter): positive thrust stop on the front flange, retention of both caps, and the strut bosses on the shell. regenerated: shell x [25.0, 97.2] vs front flange at x 28.0 and rear face at x 94.2; front lip to hub rear face 3.0 mm
M-M4 mech major One 608 is the only rotor support, ~40 mm behind the rotor CG; its radial clearance (5-12 um) allows 1.4-3.4 mrad of tilt (0.2-0.4 mm at the tip), moment loads of ~0.1-0.3 N m, a seal running on a tilting shaft and dogs loading the GL60 bell. Accepted with analysis (a second bearing does not fit the 76 mm budget): the rotor thrust pre-loads the bearing axially; tilt, tip motion, seal eccentricity and dog motion are computed in structure_v4.py and bounded by gate G5 (dial indicator with a 10 N side load); the fallback is a 698 in a 7 mm longer boss. regenerated: overhang 38 mm, tilt {'0.005': 1.4285714285714286, '0.012': 3.428571428571429} mrad, tip motion {'0.005': 0.199, '0.012': 0.4776000000000001} mm, seal eccentricity {'0.005': 0.014571428571428575, '0.012': 0.034971428571428584} mm, dog motion {'0.005': 0.013142857142857147, '0.012': 0.03154285714285716} mm vs 0.2 mm radial clearance; moments 0.072 (weight) + 0.15 (assumed inflow asymmetry) N m
M-M5 mech major The packing claim was false: the shaft was captive (collar B ahead of the bearing, circlip behind), so the nacelle with its shaft spanned 120.9 mm, not 74.9; the rotor with bolts was 61.5 mm; the ring + struts (103.7 mm) were not counted. Two-piece shaft (M5 joint ahead of the cap): the rotor assembly carries its own shaft, the stub stays in the nacelle; depths are measured from the part bounding boxes of each group, bolts included; the support set is reported separately. regenerated: rotor assembly 72.5 mm (nose plug to thread end), nacelle 74.9 mm (stub face to penetrator nut), operating 136.4 mm; support parts {'shell_top': [72.2, 112.0, 48.0], 'strut_0': [106.2, 40.3, 73.9], 'duct_1': [40.0, 195.7, 99.5]} (x, y, z extents), thickest 61 mm
M-M6 mech major Clamp, struts and ring had no fasteners or joints: the clamp halves had no lugs or holes, the ring was a single 232 x 218 mm body (no 220 mm bed takes it), the lap joints and strut-to-ring screws existed only in comments, and thrust entered the clamp by friction. Shell with 4 M4 lugs and three strut bosses (M4 heat-set inserts); three separate L-struts (identical print) whose curved feet splice the three ring joints with 4x M3 into heat-set inserts in the arcs; ring as three 120-deg arcs; all holes modelled, screws listed in the BOM (not modelled). regenerated: arc extents [40.0, 195.7, 99.5] mm (bed <= 220), strut [106.2, 40.3, 73.9] mm, shell half [72.2, 112.0, 48.0] mm; 595 part pairs clash-free
M-M7 mech major Stake socket: 16 mm engagement and 2.9 mm wall gave 9.7 MPa peak bearing pressure (> the 8 MPa wet allowable) under the 6.6 N m device moment; the 4 mm ring (0.43 mm/N in-plane compliance) and ASA shrink could close the 3.4 mm tip gap. Socket 40 mm long with a 4 mm wall under the bottom arc; ring wall 6 mm (ID 214: tip gap 5.4 mm, print at 100.5 % for shrink); tip-gap-under-load check in G10; minimum deployment depth stated. regenerated: socket bearing pressure 1.7 MPa under 7.2 N m; ring compliance 0.14 mm/N (1.10 mm per 8 N); tip gap 5.4 mm
M-M8 mech major The 0.85 inflow factor inboard of r 38 mm is optimistic for a bluff forward-facing cap step 8-15 mm behind the inner blade sections (potential-flow u/U 0.35-0.8 on the axis within one radius); 0.6-0.75 chord-averaged is more defensible, and the sharp shoulder adds ~4 N of drag at 2 m/s. Inflow factor 0.70 and 0.60 added as sensitivities and 0.70 to the pessimistic combination (the baseline sweep keeps 0.85 so the candidate ranking is unchanged: all candidates share the inboard deficit); the cap step is kept (a fairing does not fit the packing budget) and G11 tests a temporary foam fairing. regenerated: 0.70 / 0.60 give 0.94 / 0.93 W at 0.7 m/s vs baseline 0.96 W; pessimistic min self-start 0.8 m/s
M-M9 mech major Blade print orientation (pressure side down, 40 deg chord inclination at the root) rests on a 27 mm2 line with 4228 mm2 of down-facing surface inside 45 deg; 'tree supports under the leading edge' understated it. Section 9 states full support on a raft and the root-down alternative with its interlaminar stress; a printed blade is part of gate G3. root bending 1.9 MPa vs the assumed 2.7 MPa interlaminar allowable for the root-down alternative
M-M10 mech major hub_rear failed BRepCheck after STEP re-import (a zero-area cylindrical sliver from the upper pocket piece cut with clean=False) while the package reported it valid (in-memory check only). Same-domain face unification after the hub Booleans (kept only when the result is one valid solid of unchanged volume); QA gate re-imports the STEP files and runs BRepCheck. see QA_LOG_v4.md ('re-imported STEP solids pass BRepCheck')
M-M11 mech major Minimum deployable depth is ~0.3 m, not 0.15: the ring OD and the socket put the axis >= 123 mm above the bed and the ring top 109 mm above the axis; in 0.15-0.2 m streams part of the rotor is out of the water, and a leaf wrapped on one wide-chord leading edge erases the self-start margin. Minimum deployment depth computed from the geometry and stated in the report and test plan (G11); debris bar and two-point mounting recommended, not designed. regenerated: minimum depth 0.35 m
M-m1 mech minor AS568-147 (ID 69.44) on the 68.60 groove bottom is -1.2 % stretch; -146 (ID 66.27) gives +3.5 %; 'bored 72.90 H8' is the raw tube nominal (ID 72.57-73.23 with the wall tolerance). AS568-146; lands bored 73.10 H8 and the plugs resized (groove bottom recomputed). groove bottom 68.79 mm -> stretch +3.8 %, squeeze 18 %
M-m2 mech minor Circlip groove 7.4 vs DIN 471 d2 = 7.6 for d = 8; nose plug 8.9 in 9.0 is a slip fit; WetLink counterbore 20 x 6 leaves no socket room; part notes of the clamp halves were swapped; D-flat backlash ~2 deg; PTFE lip on soft 316 wears the journal. Groove 7.6; nose plug noted as slip fit + silicone; counterbore 22 mm with the nut's top 5.5 mm proud for an open-end wrench; part notes regenerated; backlash and journal hardening (hard chrome or hardened sleeve) noted in the BOM. groove d2 7.6 mm; counterbore 22.0 x 6.5 mm
M-m3 mech minor Pocket clearance 0.15 nominal measured 0.085 mm normal to the surfaces (interference in FDM practice); the tongue bolt crosses the tongue obliquely with a 2.08 mm lateral ligament; the BOM's '~17 g' blade is 24.6 g measured; the pocket wall (17.5 mm measured) made the root-chord <= 52 mm constraint unnecessarily tight. 11. Practical prototype testing plan

See docs/TEST_PLAN_v4.md (12 gates). The four measurements that close the model, in order of their effect on the 0.5-0.7 m/s prediction: G1 generator constants and cogging, G2 breakaway and running friction of the sealed shaft, G6 standstill torque of the printed rotor, G8 the power curve in a real stream.

12. Bill of materials for the simplest working prototype

docs/BOM_v4.csv: 33 lines, roughly $446-903 of parts beyond the GL60 (converter choice dominates; machining prices are estimates for a job shop; no anodising, battery, cable beyond 3 m or instrumentation). The four machined parts (shaft, two caps, tube ends) are the only non-printed, non-COTS items.

14. Unresolved assumptions

  • GL60: KV / Kt / R convention, cogging torque (the single biggest unknown for self-start), no-load loss, lead exit, which hole pattern is the stator's.
  • Hydrofoil polars at Re 4e4-8e4 come from an XFOIL surrogate; the transition Reynolds number of a wet printed surface is the dominant uncertainty at 0.5-0.6 m/s (Re/1.5 case).
  • The rotor runs at axial induction 0.4-0.6 over the outer third of the blade, where the empirical high-induction correction (Buhl baseline; Glauert-Spera and uncorrected momentum as alternatives) is load-bearing.
  • The starting-torque model (BEM at TSR 0.1 baseline; no-induction estimate as upper bound) decides the self-start verdict; neither is validated by data at this scale.
  • Converter fixed overhead (0.13 W assumed; 0.1-0.3 W plausible) decides the 0.5-0.6 m/s output; the KV convention (21.5 vs ~26 rectified) is unverified.
  • Seal and bearing friction (assumed from diameter scaling of catalogue-class values), converter efficiency curve and minimum input voltage, quiescent draw.
  • Nacelle inflow deficit (15 % inboard of r 38 mm assumed; the review's potential-flow estimate for the bluff cap step is 0.6-0.75, carried as a sensitivity and in the pessimistic combination: 0.94 / 0.93 W at 0.7 m/s for 0.70 / 0.60 against 0.96 W), guard-ring and shallow-water effects (G11), turbulence and debris.
  • WetLink dry-side geometry (a 12 x 3 mm inner protrusion is assumed in the model; the 4.5 mm stator-to-cap gap and the splice pocket depend on it).
  • Single rotor bearing tilt (G5) and the minimum deployment depth with the stake socket below the ring.
  • Manufacturer pages were unreachable: WetLink, Genasun GVB-8, LT8390 modules and seal part numbers must be confirmed before ordering.
